theme.title: Banner 18
theme.subtitle: Boston, 2023–24
theme.recap: The Celtics led the league by a mile, lost three playoff games and won the franchise's 18th title.

questions.prompt: What was Boston's regular-season win total in its 2023–24 title season?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Celtics had the best record (64–18) in the NBA

funFacts.text: It was Boston's first season without veteran guard Marcus Smart since 2014; the longtime Celtic had been traded that summer.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This was the Celtics' first season without veteran Celtic and point guard Marcus Smart since 2014.

funFacts.text: Boston also acquired Jrue Holiday from Portland in a major offseason deal that sent Malcolm Brogdon and Robert Williams III away.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Celtics sent guard Malcolm Brogdon, center/forward Robert Williams III

funFacts.text: Even the dominant Celtics had an early exit in the NBA's first In-Season Tournament: Indiana eliminated them in the quarterfinals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they were eliminated from the tournament with a loss to the Indiana Pacers in the quarterfinals.

questions.prompt: Boston won the 2024 title. How many playoff games did it lose along the way?
questions.note: Three. Only the 2017 Warriors lost fewer since the four best-of-seven rounds began.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: With a playoff record of 16–3, the Celtics were second only to the 2016–17 Golden State Warriors

funFacts.text: Boston eliminated both Miami and Cleveland in five-game playoff series before reaching the Eastern Conference finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Celtics dispatched the Miami Heat and Cleveland Cavaliers in five games each

funFacts.text: Kristaps Porziņģis missed almost the entire Eastern Conference playoff run before rejoining the team for the Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Upon reaching the Finals, Porziņģis returned to action after missing nearly the entire playoffs up until that point.

funFacts.text: Boston and Dallas had never met in a playoff series before the 2024 Finals, despite both teams' long histories.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This was the first playoff meeting between the Celtics and the Mavericks

questions.prompt: Jaylen Brown won 2024 Finals MVP. What did he average in the series?
questions.context: 2024 NBA Finals · five games vs Dallas

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: after averaging 20.8 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 5.0 assists per game

funFacts.text: Kristaps Porziņģis came back after 38 days without a game and gave Boston a jolt off the bench in the Finals opener.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: after not playing in a game for 38 days and recorded 20 points, six rebounds and three blocks off the bench

funFacts.text: Brown and Jayson Tatum both scored at least 30 in Game 3, only the second such Finals pairing in Celtics franchise history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: It was the second time in franchise history that two players each scored 30-plus points in a Finals game.

funFacts.text: Brown contributed eight rebounds and eight assists in Game 3, when Boston withstood a late rally from Dallas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Brown had eight rebounds and eight assists

questions.prompt: How old was Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla when he reached the 2024 Finals?
questions.note: 35, in his second season as Boston’s head coach.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the 35-year-old head coach appointed by the Celtics a season prior

funFacts.text: Before he coached the Celtics, Mazzulla played point guard for West Virginia University.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He played college basketball for the West Virginia Mountaineers as a point guard.

funFacts.text: Mazzulla became Boston's interim head coach after Ime Udoka's suspension, then earned the full-time position.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Mazzulla was named the interim head coach of the Celtics after head coach Ime Udoka was suspended for the entire season.

funFacts.text: As a college freshman, Mazzulla helped West Virginia win the 2007 National Invitation Tournament under John Beilein.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: As a freshman at West Virginia, Mazzulla helped the team win the 2007 National Invitation Tournament under coach John Beilein.

questions.prompt: By how many games did Boston finish ahead of the East's second seed in 2023–24?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: widest margin of wins between the first and second seeds in the Eastern Conference since 1976 at 14 games

funFacts.text: The New York Knicks were Boston's closest challenger in both the Atlantic Division and the entire Eastern Conference.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the second-place team in the Atlantic Division and the entire Eastern Conference, the New York Knicks.

funFacts.text: Boston secured home-court advantage throughout the playoffs after defeating Oklahoma City in early April.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: clinching the best record in the NBA and securing a home-court advantage throughout the entire playoffs

funFacts.text: Boston's home crowd averaged more than 19,000 fans per regular-season game at TD Garden.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Celtics drew an average home attendance of 19,156 in 41 home games in the 2023–24 NBA season.
